I'll construct a query to solve this problem, assuming tables like `customer`, `rental`, `payment`, `inventory`, and `film`. WITH FirstRental AS (
    SELECT
        p.customer_id,
        p.rental_id,
        r.inventory_id,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY p.customer_id ORDER BY p.payment_date) as rn
    FROM payment p
    JOIN rental r ON p.rental_id = r.rental_id
),
FirstMovieRating AS (
    SELECT
        fr.customer_id,
        f.rating
    FROM FirstRental fr
    JOIN inventory i ON fr.inventory_id = i.inventory_id
    JOIN film f ON i.film_id = f.film_id
    WHERE fr.rn = 1
),
CustomerStats AS (
    SELECT
        p.customer_id,
        SUM(p.amount) as total_amount,
        COUNT(p.rental_id) as total_rentals
    FROM payment p
    GROUP BY p.customer_id
)
SELECT
    fmr.rating,
    AVG(cs.total_amount) as avg_total_amount,
    AVG(cs.total_rentals - 1) as avg_subsequent_rentals
FROM FirstMovieRating fmr
JOIN CustomerStats cs ON fmr.customer_id = cs.customer_id
GROUP BY fmr.rating
ORDER BY fmr.rating
